name: Justin Kennedy

summary.text: Justin Kennedy, a son of retired Supreme Court Justice Anthony Kennedy, ran Deutsche Bank's real estate capital markets business during a period when, according to New York Times reporting cited by other outlets, the bank became Donald Trump's most important lender and extended well over $1 billion in loans for his New York and Chicago skyscraper projects. He worked in the commercial real estate division, not the private wealth unit that later lent to Trump.

facts.claim: Justin Kennedy ran Deutsche Bank's real estate capital markets work; during his tenure the bank became Donald Trump's most important lender, extending well over $1 billion in loans for skyscraper projects in New York and Chicago, according to reporting originating with the New York Times.
facts.quote: During his tenure, Deutsche Bank became Mr. Trump's most important lender, dispensing well over $1 billion in loans to him for the renovation and construction of skyscrapers in New York and Chicago.

facts.claim: Former Deutsche Bank employee Stephanie Ruhle said much of the Trump lending came from the bank's private bank, where Kennedy did not work, and that most of the recent private-bank lending occurred after Kennedy had left the bank.
facts.quote: A lot of this comes from multiple sides of the bank, specifically the private bank, and that was not where Mr. Kennedy worked.

openQuestions: The site labels Kennedy 'Head of DB Real Estate Securitization' and groups him with the private-wealth lending of 2011–2016. Sources describe him as running real estate capital markets and say the private-bank lending largely post-dated his departure; the exact title and dates of his tenure were not confirmed.
The original New York Times article (June 2018) is the primary account; it was not reachable from this environment.
